correctness.rationale: For finite undirected connected G, symmetric edge rings conserve the mean and reduce centered energy by 2 mu(1-mu) times squared endpoint difference. The graph spectral gap gives an exponential expected-energy decay at rate 2 alpha mu(1-mu) lambda_2. Integrating against independent first site-refresh time Exp(n) and applying Markov at squared threshold margin yields the displayed bound. Strict common-side regions are invariant and absorb a.s. A two-event lower-bound route on the two-site graph has exact probability alpha/(alpha+2)^2 and produces a mean below theta, after which the same theorem guarantees wrong fixation with probability approaching one. This proves the inverse-rate lower order. General absorption follows by a finite positive-probability path from each binary vector after a site-refresh sweep. Exact rational edge-energy and example algebra were replayed with the stand-alone checker; no finite census substitutes for these general arguments.

value.rationale: A graph-topological reliability inequality answers how quickly dispersal must outpace local threshold events before the metapopulation initial mean predicts expansion versus extinction, with explicit network connectivity and heterogeneity dependence. The two-patch matching-order event establishes a sharp natural rate boundary and distinguishes the result from mere qualitative homogenization. The model is an idealized threshold-refresh process, not a field-calibrated demographic model.
